newsitem.title: USA: Cunanan tipster rewarded by New York gay group.
newsitem.headline: Cunanan tipster rewarded by New York gay group.

text.p: The Miami houseboat caretaker who stumbled upon the suspected killer of fashion designer Gianni Versace was given a $10,000 reward on Monday by a New York group devoted to stopping violence against gays and lesbians.

Amid a crush of TV crews and reporters, Fernando Carreira, 71, received a large cardboard check from the Gay and Lesbian Anti-Violence Project in a Greenwich Village park in the heart of New York's gay community. Owners of the famous Stonewall Bar on Christopher Street contributed $2,500 to the reward.

Carreira, who is suing the city of Miami Beach and Dade County claiming $65,000 in rewards posted by various agencies, last Wednesday led police to the houseboat where the body of alleged murderer Andrew Cunanan was found with a self-inflicted gunshot wound.
Cunanan was on the FBI's 10 Most Wanted list for four killings across the United States before he allegedly gunned down Versace on July 15 in front of his Miami Beach mansion.

"Although the remarkable action Mr Carreira took last week didn't actually lead to the conviction of Mr Cunanan, we believe that they were responsible actions, publicly-minded actions," the Project's executive director Christine Quinn told reporters. "We decided not to stand on detail."
Quinn said there were six serial killers who had murdered 35 gay men in the United States since 1992 and she charged that the FBI had not become involved when asked to by her group.
"Tragically, we need to put up rewards," she said.

Three out of five of Cunanan's victims were gay men, causing tension in gay communities such as those in New York and San Francisco. Cunanan also was gay and described by his mother and acquaintances as a high-class prostitute.
"I want to say thank you and that I appreciate very much what your organisation has done," Carreira said as he accepted the reward. "You promise and you go through with your promise."

Then, holding up a leaflet bearing six photographs of Cunanan in various guises, he said to cheers from spectators, "About this, case closed." Carreira said he had some debts to pay, but had otherwise not decided how to spend the money.

Carreira was on his weekly caretaking rounds with his wife last Wednesday when he went aboard the two-story houseboat and saw signs that someone was sleeping there, including a pair of sandals on the floor. He drew his gun, and ran when he heard the shot from the upstairs bedroom where Cunanan was later found dead.
